reason: Round 1: three agents on the routes Kimi K3.1 Pro chose (pairs, boost, forest; oversight/round-1.json), at once, in the sandbox and under the file trace (live/synth-r1-*). All three finished inside the 40-minute wall clock and every trail checks. Each ran the inherited analysis pilot-only first (baseline, cv_auc 0.6313), then a pilot-only estimate, then scored the held-out file once: pairs at step-17 (holdout_auc 0.8923, cv 0.8923), boost at step-22 (0.8538, cv 0.8343), forest at step-22 (0.8983, cv 0.8931). floor is reached three times. Every candidate propose drafted is accepted. One judgment: forest-cv was reached by a random forest on the raw features (cv 0.8152, step-13), but forest-holdout by a random forest on the raw features and all 78 pairwise products (step-20), which the agent built after reading the pairs route's result through project_map. That is still a random forest chosen on pilot data alone, so the credit stands, and it is the method claim a reader should know. Excused reads: forest step-4 and pairs step-4 counted both data files' rows (wc -l) while looking around; each is excused where a credit rests on it. pairs' held-out run reports a gap of exactly 0: its cv_auc and holdout_auc agree to four places, which replicate.py's re-run, where cv_auc stays 0.8923 and holdout_auc changes, shows is a coincidence and not one copied from the other.
